page: The Vultr vx1-m-96c-768gb is a high-density, memory-optimized instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by AMD processors, paired with 768.0 GB of system memory. This architecture establishes an 8.0 GB per core ratio, categorizing the configuration firmly within memory-intensive operational domains. The instance provides 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. It contains no hardware GPU accelerators.

The hardware configuration is characterized by a balance of massive multi-threaded compute capability and extensive memory capacity. With 96 dedicated cores, the instance avoids shared-core contention, ensuring consistent execution for parallel compute threads. A notable architectural limitation is the minimal local NVMe SSD capacity of 1 GB, which necessitates reliance on network-attached storage or external volume architectures for persistent data storage. From an efficiency perspective, the platform consolidates high compute core counts and massive memory footprints into a single instance, optimizing resource allocation for large-scale monolithic or highly centralized architectures without incurring accelerator overhead.

The Vultr vx1-m-96c-768gb is architecturally configured for memory-bound and heavily multi-threaded workloads. Common deployment targets include large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise in-memory analytics, large batch ETL data pipelines, and memory-intensive compilation or simulation tasks that require vast RAM spaces alongside significant CPU concurrency.
